items.title: Unions push for pro-worker AI laws: “We can win them by learning from one another”
items.summary: Collective bargaining is workers’ strongest tool to make sure the benefits of artificial intelligence are shared and its excesses curbed. However, only 13 per cent of workers in Massachusetts have a union contract, Chrissy Lynch, President of the Massachusetts AFL-CIO, told union leaders at UNI Global Union’s second AI forum in Nyon on 10 November. items.title: US Department of Labor announces final rule clarifying employee, independent contractor status under federal wage and hour laws
items.summary: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division today announced a final rule to revise its analysis for distinguishing between employees and independent contractors under the Fair Labor Standards Act and two related federal laws. The new final rule provides clarity to businesses and workers alike, as well as the division’s enforcement personnel.U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling, Wage and Hour Division Administrator Andrew Rogers, and other department officials hosted an event to formally announce the final rule at the Frances Perkins Building this morning. Employers, business associations, worker advocates, independent contractors, and other stakeholders were in attendance as Secretary Sonderling highlighted the clarity and simplicity of the new regulations.The final rule rescinds an earlier 2024 rule addressing the classification of employees and independent contractors and replaces it with an analysis that is substantially similar to the framework adopted by the department in 2021. items.title: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report
items.summary: In the week ending November 14, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 203,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level. The previous week's level was revised up by 2,000 from 200,000 to 202,000. The 4-week moving average was 197,750, an increase of 2,000 from the previous week's revised average. The previous week's average was revised up by 500 from 195,250 to 195,750.

items.title: Unions in 19 countries to governments: stop handing Amazon public money while it breaks workers’ rights
items.summary: Trade union leaders from 19 countries representing millions of workers have called on governments to stop awarding public contracts to Amazon and Amazon Web Services (AWS), after a year in which US federal agencies committed more than US$3.5 billion to AWS.
